module_title: Major Crops and Producing States - Basic Superlatives
introduction: India is an agricultural powerhouse. Due to diverse soil types and climates, a wide variety of crops are grown here. For competitive exams, memorizing the top producing states for major food and cash crops is the absolute first step.

core_concepts.title: Rice
core_concepts.description: It is the most important (Number 1) food crop in India. 'West Bengal' is the largest producer, followed closely by Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

core_concepts.title: Wheat
core_concepts.description: The main food crop in North and North-Western India. 'Uttar Pradesh' is the largest producer, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Punjab.

core_concepts.title: Sugarcane
core_concepts.description: A major cash crop. 'Uttar Pradesh' is the undisputed largest producer of sugarcane in India, followed by Maharashtra.

core_concepts.title: Cotton
core_concepts.description: An important fibre crop, often called 'White Gold'. It grows best in the black soil of the Deccan Plateau. 'Gujarat' and 'Maharashtra' are the top producers.

important_entities.name: Tea
important_entities.significance: Tea is a major plantation crop. 'Assam' holds a near-monopoly, producing over half of India's tea. West Bengal (Darjeeling) comes second.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume Punjab is the largest producer of wheat and rice. Remember: Punjab leads in 'Yield per Hectare' (Productivity), but in terms of 'Total Production', UP (Wheat) and West Bengal (Rice) are Number 1.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lock in these absolute top rankings. UP dominates the northern plains for both wheat and sugarcane.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions are extremely common: Cotton -> Gujarat/Maharashtra; Tea -> Assam.
Always remember that India is the 'second-largest' producer of both Rice and Wheat in the world (behind China).
